name: Dark Soft Blue-Violet
lede: Dark Soft Blue-Violet is a dusky, muted blue-violet, one of Robert Ridgway's many modifier compounds built directly onto a base hue he had already named Soft Blue-Violet.

sections.title: A modifier chain, not a new story
sections.body: Dark Soft Blue-Violet stacks two modifiers, *dark* and *soft*, onto [[blue-violet|Blue-Violet]], the way Robert Ridgway built most of his 1912 color atlas [1]. He plotted it on plate XXIII, hue 55 prime, tone k, beside [[soft-blue-violet|Soft Blue-Violet]], the lighter step in the same column [1]. The ISCC-NBS dictionary filed the exact name again in 1955, block 200, calling it a moderate purplish blue [2]. Our own color graph puts its nearest independent neighbors at [[twilight]], [[sailor-blue]] and [[dusk]], all within 3.4 CIEDE2000 units [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this hue, as photographed, in 20 of 23,781 paintings, 0.08 percent, rarer than 69 percent of the named colors we track [4]. The earliest dated match is Fra Angelico's *Coronation of the Virgin*, from 1420, 492 years before Ridgway's 1912 plate; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [4]. Inside a painting it most often sits in shadow, in 56 percent of its 9 strongest matches [4].

origin.named_after: the base color Blue-Violet, by way of Ridgway's own modifier 'dark soft'
